_why: ADR Prism 026 §3.3 palier 3 / Pulsar issue #121 resolution criterion 3: the
coverage of the capability-contract gate is an EXPLICIT, VERSIONED list, not
whatever the probe happens to walk on the day. The probe cross-checks itself
against this file and FAILS on drift in either direction:
- a listed subject that was NOT driven  -> the gate silently lost coverage;
- a driven subject that is NOT listed   -> this artefact went stale.
Removing a line from `subjects` therefore cannot happen by accident: it must
also be removed from the probe, which makes it a visible diff. That diff
failing REVIEW is the human control the ADR asks for -- it is deliberately
not a test (a test cannot tell a legitimate retirement from an amputation).

_denominator.source: docs/PROTOCOL.md -- the count Pulsar advertises as its v5 surface.
note: GetVersion on a -Full build reports a larger availableRequests array (151)
because it includes the pulsar: vendor requests and the handlers upstream
registers but PROTOCOL.md does not advertise. 137 stays the denominator so
the ratio keeps meaning the same thing across builds.

_cross_check_note: Requests used ONLY as the independent re-query for someone else's verdict.
They are exercised for real (a broken one breaks the verdict it backs), but
they are not the subject under test, so they are not gated by name.

deliberately_uncovered.RemoveInput: Known red, see `open_findings_routed_out` below. Uncovered because the defect is real and unfixed, not because it is uninteresting -- it is the first thing to re-gate once the fix lands.
deliberately_uncovered.PauseRecord before the first written byt: Known red, see `open_findings_routed_out` below. The healthy pause/resume path IS gated (Record family); only the wedge-triggering precondition is out.
deliberately_uncovered.Profiles / SceneCollections: Pulsar is headless and boots one implicit profile+collection; Prism never drives these. No consumer, no gate -- covering them would test upstream, not Pulsar.
deliberately_uncovered.Hotkeys: No input device in a headless service; TriggerHotkeyByName has no consumer in Prism. Same reasoning as above.
deliberately_uncovered.MediaInput cursor: SetMediaInputCursor / OffsetMediaInputCursor / TriggerMediaInputAction need a real ffmpeg_source with a media file; the fixture cost is real and no Prism path drives them today. Next candidate after the ones below.
deliberately_uncovered.SplitRecordFile / CreateRecordChapter: Both are format-conditional (fragmented mp4 / hybrid mp4) and would need their own record-format fixture. Left out of this pass on cost, not on principle.
deliberately_uncovered.SetSceneItemIndex / SetSceneItemBlendMod: Same family as the two SceneItem subjects already gated; adding them is mechanical and is exactly the kind of widening the ADR calls a separate job.
deliberately_uncovered.Projectors / Dialogs (Open*Projector, Op: Qt frontend surface. Pulsar runs QT_QPA_PLATFORM=minimal with no UI; these are structurally inapplicable.
deliberately_uncovered.pulsar: vendor requests: Multi-stream (pulsar:StartDestination) and pulsar:GetCapabilities have their own dedicated probes (probe-multi-stream.py, live-test.yml). Not re-litigated here.

RemoveInput reports success and removes: 2026-07-27 Forge/#121 -- NEW, and the same shape as #119. RemoveInput
answers result=true, and 3 s later the input is still in GetInputList AND
its scene item is still in GetSceneItemList. The v5 contract for this
request is explicit ('will immediately remove all associated scene
items'); nothing of the sort happens. The source only really goes away
when the scene holding it is removed.
Probable root cause, to confirm: obs_source_remove() only flags the
source and emits the 'remove' signal -- in obs-studio it is the FRONTEND
that reacts and deletes the scene items. Pulsar's frontend stub has no
such handler, so the signal lands nowhere. Exactly the #119 pattern
(a stub that does not close a loop libobs expects the frontend to close).
NOT gated: this is a pre-existing red that palier 2 never covered, and
wiring the gate onto it would make the gate red on day one. Routed to
Atlas/Eleven as a candidate issue -- reproducible in 6 requests.
PauseRecord before the muxer's first byt: 2026-07-27 Forge/#121 -- reproduced while wiring this gate. PauseRecord
issued while GetRecordStatus.outputBytes is still 0 (i.e. immediately
after StartRecord reports outputActive) leaves the ffmpeg_muxer wedged:
SaveReplayBuffer then never produces a file, and StopReplayBuffer /
StopRecord answer Success() while outputActive stays true. That last part
is a #120-class honesty gap -- the effect verification does not catch it
because the output really is 'stopping', it just never stops.
Trigger is exotic (no Prism path pauses a recording that has not started
writing), and the same sequence with the recording actually producing
data is clean, so this is NOT gated here: widening a gate onto a known
red is exactly what ADR Prism 026 §3.3 forbids. Routed to Atlas/Eleven
as a candidate issue, with a live repro, rather than silenced.
Likely upstream (obs ffmpeg_muxer pause-before-first-packet), to confirm.
SetStreamServiceSettings has no effect o: is what this probe gates), but obs_frontend_streaming_start() never binds
single-stream StartStream path is therefore structurally unreachable in
Pulsar; the live path is the pulsar:StartDestination multi-stream API.
This is NOT silenced: StartStream is gated here and must answer with an
EXPLICIT refusal (post-#120 behaviour, which it does). Whether the v5 path
should be wired, or SetStreamServiceSettings should refuse instead of
reporting a success the output can never honour, is an architecture call --
routed to Atlas, not decided by the gate.
